judgements.name: the central lens
judgements.alternative: the retired 45/15/20/20 blend of four lenses
judgements.why: three of the four blended lenses value a developer on reported earnings and historical-cost book, which for a company whose worth sits in an undelivered order book measures a floor; and the weights had never cleared any out-of-sample test

judgements.name: the discount rate's shape
judgements.adopted: a schedule gliding to a norm-built terminal
judgements.alternative: a flat rate held for the whole window
judgements.why: the central bank publishes a disinflation path and this study's own cost-of-debt assumptions already follow it; a flat crisis rate for fifteen years is a forecast that Egypt never normalises, and it was never argued for

judgements.name: the length of the explicit window
judgements.alternative: five years, as the earlier editions carried
judgements.why: a window that ends at 44% growth and then capitalises at 7% capitalises a rate the model never reached; it put 74% of value in the terminal

judgements.name: terminal growth
judgements.why: 12% against a terminal rate embedding about 14.6% inflation is a perpetual real decline of two to three points a year that nothing disclosed supports

judgements.name: the delivery path
judgements.adopted: the disclosed 15% run, faded to nothing over ten years
judgements.alternative: the 15% run held flat across the window
judgements.why: a company cannot hand over 15% more homes every year for ever: it is limited by what it can build, and holding the run flat would have deliveries fourteen times higher in 2040 than in 2026
